import os, sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())
import sqlite3
from src.repository import initialize, list_contacts
from src.service import add_contact, import_contacts
from src.api import handle_add, handle_import

def fresh():
    c = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
    initialize(c)
    return c

def raises(fn, *args):
    try:
        fn(*args)
    except ValueError:
        return True
    return False

# empty batch
c = fresh()
assert import_contacts(c, []) == {"inserted": 0, "updated": 0}
assert list_contacts(c) == []

# insert + normalization + trimming
c = fresh()
assert import_contacts(c, [{"email": "  A@B.com ", "name": "  Alice "}, {"email": "b@x.io", "name": "Bob"}]) == {"inserted": 2, "updated": 0}
assert list_contacts(c) == [("a@b.com", "Alice"), ("b@x.io", "Bob")]

# existing email counted as updated even if name unchanged
assert import_contacts(c, [{"email": "a@b.com", "name": "Alice"}, {"email": "new@x.io", "name": "N"}]) == {"inserted": 1, "updated": 1}
assert list_contacts(c) == [("a@b.com", "Alice"), ("b@x.io", "Bob"), ("new@x.io", "N")]

# add_contact and list_contacts still work
add_contact(c, "z@z.z", "Zed")
assert ("z@z.z", "Zed") in list_contacts(c)

# validation failures leave data unchanged
before = list_contacts(c)
bad_batches = [
    [{"email": "ok@x.io", "name": "Ok"}, "not-a-dict"],
    [{"email": "ok@x.io", "name": "Ok"}, {"email": "a@b.com", "name": "A", "extra": 1}],
    [{"email": "ok@x.io", "name": "Ok"}, {"email": "a@b.com"}],
    [{"email": "ok@x.io", "name": "Ok"}, {"email": "a@@b", "name": "A"}],
    [{"email": "ok@x.io", "name": "Ok"}, {"email": "@b", "name": "A"}],
    [{"email": "ok@x.io", "name": "Ok"}, {"email": "a@", "name": "A"}],
    [{"email": "ok@x.io", "name": "Ok"}, {"email": "a b@x.io", "name": "A"}],
    [{"email": "ok@x.io", "name": "Ok"}, {"email": "a@x.io", "name": "   "}],
    [{"email": "ok@x.io", "name": "Ok"}, {"email": 5, "name": "A"}],
    [{"email": "ok@x.io", "name": "Ok"}, {"email": "dup@x.io", "name": "A"}, {"email": " DUP@x.io", "name": "B"}],
]
for batch in bad_batches:
    assert raises(import_contacts, c, batch), batch
    assert list_contacts(c) == before

# non-list rows
assert raises(import_contacts, c, "abc")

# database failure mid-batch rolls back everything
class FailingConn:
    def __init__(self, inner, fail_on):
        self.inner = inner; self.fail_on = fail_on; self.calls = 0
    def execute(self, sql, params=()):
        if sql.startswith("INSERT"):
            self.calls += 1
            if self.calls == self.fail_on:
                raise sqlite3.OperationalError("boom")
        return self.inner.execute(sql, params)
    def __enter__(self): return self.inner.__enter__()
    def __exit__(self, *a): return self.inner.__exit__(*a)

c = fresh()
add_contact(c, "keep@x.io", "Keep")
before = list_contacts(c)
try:
    import_contacts(FailingConn(c, 2), [{"email": "p@x.io", "name": "P"}, {"email": "q@x.io", "name": "Q"}, {"email": "keep@x.io", "name": "Changed"}])
    raise AssertionError("expected failure")
except sqlite3.OperationalError:
    pass
assert list_contacts(c) == before

# API envelope
c = fresh()
assert handle_import(c, {"contacts": [{"email": "a@b.co", "name": "A"}]}) == {"inserted": 1, "updated": 0}
assert handle_import(c, {"contacts": []}) == {"inserted": 0, "updated": 0}
assert raises(handle_import, c, [])
assert raises(handle_import, c, {})
assert raises(handle_import, c, {"contacts": "x"})
assert raises(handle_import, c, {"contacts": [], "extra": 1})
assert handle_add(c, {"email": "e@x.io", "name": "E"}) == {"ok": True}
print("ok")
